summary:
Starting pitcher is the category to build around right now — every rating (R1 through R4) is a perfect 3-0 (100%) over the last 14 days with active 3-game win streaks, a clean signal across the board rather than noise in one model. Flip side: bullpen_fatigue is ice cold everywhere, 0-3 across all four ratings with matching 5-game losing streaks. That split tells you exactly where to lean today — trust the SP-driven pick, fade anything that's only supported by bullpen_fatigue. R4 remains the sharpest tool in the shed on volume context, sitting at 64% (119-68, +63.0u) for the season on strong plays and already 2-1 the last two weeks, so when R4 and SP both point the same direction on tonight's card, that's your green light. The category combo data backs this up structurally too — trends+sp leads all pairings at 58.0% (370-268, n=638), so any game where trends and starting pitcher agree deserves full weight tonight.

On the board, keep an eye on where these hot signals intersect with the proven team trends. LAD remains the model's best friend when liked — 70% straight up (39-17) and a blistering 80% on strong plays (+27.0u) — so if LAD shows up with an SP-driven strong play tonight, that's about as clean a convergence as this model offers. BOS (70%, strong 76% +19.0u) and TBR (70%, strong 70% +21.0u) sit in the same tier; any slate appearance from either name with trends+sp agreement should be treated as a premium look. Conversely, fade NYY on volume — 49% straight up and a losing -4.0u on strong plays is the one red flag among high-frequency teams, so even if a rating likes them today, size down unless SP and trends both confirm independently. With all four ratings moving in lockstep on both the hot (SP) and cold (bullpen_fatigue) sides, today's biggest edge isn't about which rating to trust — it's about which category each rating is leaning on.
